title: Embeddings client: unified stream adapter, typed error contract, and adaptive pagination
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Background: Customers are integrating large-scale embedding and reranking pipelines and report divergent behavior between our Python and TypeScript SDKs: inconsistent streaming semantics, opaque HTTP error handling, and difficulty resuming large result scans. This ticket unifies the client surface so that both languages share a single stream adapter concept, a documented typed error contract, and an adaptive pagination strategy that improves latency and cost for mixed-size workloads.

Problem statement:
- TS and Py SDKs expose different streaming APIs (EventEmitter vs async iterator) causing duplicate server-side compatibility guards and confusing docs.
- Errors returned during long scans (rate limits, transient GPU OOMs, partial shard failures) are currently opaque or surfaced as raw HTTP status codes; customers must implement fragile retry logic.
- Large result sets waste latency/cost when page sizes are static; small page sizes increase wall-time due to more round trips.

Goals:
1) Introduce a language-agnostic stream adapter pattern (async generator in TS + AsyncIterator/async for in Python) with the same event framing and resume token semantics.
2) Define a stable typed error contract (RetryableError, ClientInputError, QuotaExceededError, ServerTransientError, PermanentServerError) across transports and map HTTP codes and body shapes to those types. Publish mapping table in SDK docs.
3) Implement adaptive page sizing in client that adjusts page_size based on recent payload density and latency targets, with optional customer controls.
4) Provide safe resume semantics using opaque resume tokens that can recover from mid-scan failures without re-requesting previous pages.
5) Maintain backwards-compatibility via a compatibility adapter layer and deprecate the old callback API after one release.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes EmbeddingsStream async iterator with documented framing and resume_token field
TypeScript SDK exposes identical async generator semantics and a unified Response shape in @redwood/embeddings package
Error mappings documented with examples and mapped in code: 429->RetryableError, 503/504->ServerTransientError, 400->ClientInputError, 402->QuotaExceededError, 500->PermanentServerError
Adaptive pagination reduces median completion latency by >=15% on mixed document workloads in internal benchmark and reduces average token cost per query by >=8% for targeted workloads
Resume tokens allow complete scan resume after transient failure in 95% of injected failure experiments (internal chaos test)
All changes have unit tests and integration tests, plus migration guide and changelog entry
Docs updated with examples (Python/TS) and breaking-change timeline for deprecated callback API
tasks: Design stream adapter framing and protocol (w/ resume_token and chunk metadata)
Implement TypeScript async generator and new Response types in @redwood/embeddings
Implement Python AsyncIterator and TypedDict/dataclass response shapes
Add error mapping layer in client transport and centralize in common package
Implement adaptive pagination heuristic and expose tunables (min_page, max_page, latency_target_ms)
Server-side: add optional resume_token emission and small compatibility shim for older backends
Benchmarks and chaos tests: run mixed-size workloads (short, medium, long) and inject 429/503/connection resets
Release branch and rollout plan with feature flag gating

notes: Technical decision: Use small envelope with header:{resume_token, chunk_index, page_checksum, vector_precision} and payload: binary-encoded concatenated vectors to minimize JSON overhead.
Compatibility: Add compatibility adapter that will accept newline-delimited JSON and translate to new envelope for older servers. Deprecate old API in next major minor release.
Retry policy: SDK will expose default backoff with jitter for RetryableError and allow customers to provide custom RetryPolicy objects (TS generics / Py protocol).
Typing: TS will export EmbeddingResponse<TVector = number[]> generic; Python will export EmbeddingResponseTyped = TypedDict('EmbeddingResponseTyped', {...}) and a dataclass variant for ergonomic use.
Telemetry: Emit token_density and average_vector_size as metrics to help Optimize suggest quantization or batching profiles.
